title.en: Linear First-Order Equations, Integrating Factors & Nonlinear Reductions
title.ar: المعادلات الخطية من الرتبة الأولى وعوامل التكامل ومعادلات برنولي

body.en: While Chapter 1 addressed separable equations where rates factor into independent coordinate components, physical systems routinely combine internal dissipation with external driving forces: thermal cooling under active heating, inductive-resistive electrical circuits under AC forcing, or chemical reactors subject to continuous inflow and outflow. Such systems are modeled by first-order linear differential equations. This chapter develops the exact integrating factor technique, analyzes transient versus steady-state dynamics, and presents nonlinear transformations including Bernoulli and Riccati equations.
body.ar: While Chapter 1 addressed separable المعادلات حيث rates factor into independent الإحداثي components, physical systems routinely combine internal dissipation with external driving forces: thermal cooling under active heating, inductive-resistive electrical circuits under AC forcing, or chemical reactors subject to continuous inflow and outflow. Such systems are modeled by first-order linear differential equations. This chapter develops the exact integrating factor technique, analyzes transient versus steady-state dynamics, and presents nonlinear transformations including Bernoulli and Riccati المعادلات.

label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — Definition 2.1: First-Order Linear Equations & Standard Normal Form
label.ar: ● Level 1 Foundation — تعريف 2.1: First-Order المعادلات الخطية & Standard Normal Form

body.en:
A first-order differential equation is linear if it can be expressed in the canonical standard form: \[ \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)\,y = Q(x), \] where \( P(x) \) and \( Q(x) \) are continuous functions on an open interval \( I \subseteq \mathbb{R} \). The equation is homogeneous if \( Q(x) \equiv 0 \); otherwise it is nonhomogeneous.

The differential operator \( L[y] = \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y \) is a linear mapping from \( C^1(I) \to C(I) \): \[ L[c_1 y_1 + c_2 y_2] = c_1 L[y_1] + c_2 L[y_2] \] for any scalars \( c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R} \). If an equation is presented with a non-constant coefficient preceding \( y' \), e.g. \( a_1(x)y' + a_0(x)y = b(x) \), it must be normalized by dividing through by \( a_1(x) \) on intervals where \( a_1(x) \neq 0 \) before computing integrating factors.
body.ar:
A first-order المعادلة التفاضلية is linear if it can be expressed in the canonical standard form: \[ \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)\,y = Q(x), \] حيث \( P(x) \) and \( Q(x) \) are continuous الدوال on an open interval \( I \subseteq \mathbb{R} \). The المعادلة is homogeneous if \( Q(x) \equiv 0 \); otherwise it is nonhomogeneous.

The differential operator \( L[y] = \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y \) is a linear mapping from \( C^1(I) \to C(I) \): \[ L[c_1 y_1 + c_2 y_2] = c_1 L[y_1] + c_2 L[y_2] \] for any scalars \( c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R} \). If an المعادلة is presented with a non-الثابت المعامل preceding \( y' \), e.g. \( a_1(x)y' + a_0(x)y = b(x) \), it must be normalized by dividing through by \( a_1(x) \) on intervals حيث \( a_1(x) \neq 0 \) before computing integrating factors.

label.en: ▲ Level 1 Foundation — Theorem 2.1: The Integrating Factor & Product Rule Inversion
label.ar: ▲ Level 1 Foundation — مبرهنة 2.1: The Integrating Factor & Product Rule Inversion

body.en: Let \( P(x) \) and \( Q(x) \) be continuous on an open interval \( I \). Define the integrating factor: \[ \mu(x) = \exp\left(\int P(x)\,dx\right). \] Then \( \mu(x) > 0 \) for all \( x \in I \), and a function \( y(x) \) is a solution to \( y' + P(x)y = Q(x) \) if and only if \[ y(x) = \frac{1}{\mu(x)}\left(\int \mu(x)Q(x)\,dx + C\right) \] for some constant \( C \in \mathbb{R} \).
body.ar: Let \( P(x) \) and \( Q(x) \) be continuous on an open interval \( I \). Define the integrating factor: \[ \mu(x) = \exp\left(\int P(x)\,dx\right). \] Then \( \mu(x) > 0 \) for all \( x \in I \), and a الدالة \( y(x) \) is a الحل to \( y' + P(x)y = Q(x) \) if and only if \[ y(x) = \frac{1}{\mu(x)}\left(\int \mu(x)Q(x)\,dx + C\right) \] for some الثابت \( C \in \mathbb{R} \).

label.ar: البرهان

body.en: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and Chain Rule, the derivative of \( \mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx} \) is: \[ \mu'(x) = P(x)e^{\int P(x)\,dx} = P(x)\mu(x). \] Multiplying the standard form \( y' + P(x)y = Q(x) \) by \( \mu(x) \): \[ \mu(x)y'(x) + \mu(x)P(x)y(x) = \mu(x)Q(x). \] Since \( \mu(x)P(x) = \mu'(x) \), the left side collapses into the exact product rule: \[ \frac{d}{dx}\big[\mu(x)y(x)\big] = \mu(x)Q(x). \] Integrating both sides with respect to \( x \): \[ \mu(x)y(x) = \int \mu(x)Q(x)\,dx + C. \] Since \( \mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx} > 0 \) is strictly positive everywhere on \( I \), dividing by \( \mu(x) \) yields the unique general solution family.
body.ar: By the Fundamental مبرهنة of التفاضل والتكامل and Chain Rule, the المشتقة of \( \mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx} \) is: \[ \mu'(x) = P(x)e^{\int P(x)\,dx} = P(x)\mu(x). \] Multiplying the standard form \( y' + P(x)y = Q(x) \) by \( \mu(x) \): \[ \mu(x)y'(x) + \mu(x)P(x)y(x) = \mu(x)Q(x). \] Since \( \mu(x)P(x) = \mu'(x) \), the left side collapses into the exact product rule: \[ \frac{d}{dx}\big[\mu(x)y(x)\big] = \mu(x)Q(x). \] Integrating both sides بالنسبة إلى \( x \): \[ \mu(x)y(x) = \int \mu(x)Q(x)\,dx + C. \] Since \( \mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx} > 0 \) is strictly positive everywhere on \( I \), dividing by \( \mu(x) \) yields the unique general الحل family.

blocks.heading: Analytical Procedure for First-Order Linear Equations

label.ar: 1. Normalization (المعادلات الخطية من الرتبة الأولى وعوامل التكامل ومعادلات برنولي)

value.en: Divide through by the leading coefficient to obtain standard form \( y' + P(x)y = Q(x) \). Identify \( P(x) \) and \( Q(x) \), including any negative signs.

label.ar: 2. Integrating Factor (المعادلات الخطية من الرتبة الأولى وعوامل التكامل ومعادلات برنولي)

value.en: Compute \( \mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx} \). Do not add a constant of integration \( +C \) here, as any scalar multiple of \( \mu(x) \) cancels.

label.ar: 3. Exact Product Collapse (المعادلات الخطية من الرتبة الأولى وعوامل التكامل ومعادلات برنولي)

value.en: Multiply the entire differential equation by \( \mu(x) \), collapsing the left side into \( \frac{d}{dx}[\mu(x)y] = \mu(x)Q(x) \).

label.ar: 4. Integration & Isolation (المعادلات الخطية من الرتبة الأولى وعوامل التكامل ومعادلات برنولي)

value.en: Integrate \( \mu(x)Q(x) \) with respect to \( x \), add the constant \( +C \), and divide the entire right side by \( \mu(x) \).

label.en: Worked example 2.A — Integrating Factor with Variable Coefficients
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.A — Integrating Factor with المتغير المعاملات

body.en:
Find the general solution of the differential equation \[ x \frac{dy}{dx} + 2y = 4x^2, \qquad x > 0. \]

Step 1: Normalize: Divide by \( x \): \[ \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{2}{x}y = 4x. \] Here \( P(x) = \frac{2}{x} \) and \( Q(x) = 4x \).

Step 2: Integrating factor: \[ \mu(x) = \exp\left(\int \frac{2}{x}\,dx\right) = \exp(2\ln x) = \exp(\ln x^2) = x^2. \]

Step 3: Multiply and integrate: \[ \frac{d}{dx}\big[x^2 y\big] = x^2(4x) = 4x^3 \implies x^2 y = \int 4x^3\,dx = x^4 + C. \]

Step 4: Isolate \( y(x) \): \[ y(x) = x^2 + \frac{C}{x^2}. \] Notice that as \( x \to 0^+ \), the homogeneous term \( C/x^2 \) diverges unless \( C = 0 \), reflecting the singularity of \( P(x) \) at \( x = 0 \).
body.ar:
Find the general الحل of the المعادلة التفاضلية \[ x \frac{dy}{dx} + 2y = 4x^2, \qquad x > 0. \]

Step 1: Normalize: Divide by \( x \): \[ \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{2}{x}y = 4x. \] Here \( P(x) = \frac{2}{x} \) and \( Q(x) = 4x \).

Step 2: Integrating factor: \[ \mu(x) = \exp\left(\int \frac{2}{x}\,dx\right) = \exp(2\ln x) = \exp(\ln x^2) = x^2. \]

Step 3: Multiply and integrate: \[ \frac{d}{dx}\big[x^2 y\big] = x^2(4x) = 4x^3 \implies x^2 y = \int 4x^3\,dx = x^4 + C. \]

Step 4: Isolate \( y(x) \): \[ y(x) = x^2 + \frac{C}{x^2}. \] Notice that as \( x \to 0^+ \), the homogeneous term \( C/x^2 \) diverges unless \( C = 0 \), reflecting the singularity of \( P(x) \) at \( x = 0 \).

label.en: Worked example 2.B — Initial Value Problems & Singular Boundary Points
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.B — Initial Value Problems & Singular Boundary Points

body.en:
Solve the initial value problem \[ \frac{dy}{dx} - \frac{2}{x}y = x^3 e^x, \qquad y(1) = 0, \quad x > 0. \]

Step 1: Integrating factor: \( P(x) = -\frac{2}{x} \), so \[ \mu(x) = \exp\left(\int -\frac{2}{x}\,dx\right) = e^{-2\ln x} = x^{-2} = \frac{1}{x^2}. \]

Step 2: Collapse and integrate: \[ \frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{y}{x^2}\right] = \frac{1}{x^2}\big(x^3 e^x\big) = x e^x. \] Integrating by parts (\( u = x, dv = e^x dx \)): \[ \frac{y}{x^2} = \int x e^x\,dx = x e^x - e^x + C = (x - 1)e^x + C. \]

Step 3: Apply initial condition \( y(1) = 0 \): \[ \frac{0}{1^2} = (1 - 1)e^1 + C \implies C = 0. \]

Step 4: Particular solution: \[ y(x) = x^2(x - 1)e^x. \]
body.ar:
Solve the initial value problem \[ \frac{dy}{dx} - \frac{2}{x}y = x^3 e^x, \qquad y(1) = 0, \quad x > 0. \]

Step 1: Integrating factor: \( P(x) = -\frac{2}{x} \), so \[ \mu(x) = \exp\left(\int -\frac{2}{x}\,dx\right) = e^{-2\ln x} = x^{-2} = \frac{1}{x^2}. \]

Step 2: Collapse and integrate: \[ \frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{y}{x^2}\right] = \frac{1}{x^2}\big(x^3 e^x\big) = x e^x. \] Integrating by parts (\( u = x, dv = e^x dx \)): \[ \frac{y}{x^2} = \int x e^x\,dx = x e^x - e^x + C = (x - 1)e^x + C. \]

Step 3: Apply initial condition \( y(1) = 0 \): \[ \frac{0}{1^2} = (1 - 1)e^1 + C \implies C = 0. \]

Step 4: Particular الحل: \[ y(x) = x^2(x - 1)e^x. \]

label.en: Worked example 2.C — Analytical Application: Dynamic Inflow-Outflow Mixing Tanks
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.C — Analytical Application: Dynamic Inflow-Outflow Mixing Tanks

body.en:
A tank initially contains \( V_0 = 100 \text{ L} \) of fresh water. Brine with salt concentration \( c_{\text{in}} = 0.5 \text{ kg/L} \) flows in at \( r_{\text{in}} = 4 \text{ L/min} \). Well-mixed solution is pumped out at \( r_{\text{out}} = 2 \text{ L/min} \). Determine the total salt mass \( Q(t) \) in the tank as a function of time.

Step 1: Dynamic volume: Because \( r_{\text{in}} \neq r_{\text{out}} \), volume changes with time: \[ V(t) = V_0 + (r_{\text{in}} - r_{\text{out}})t = 100 + 2t. \]

Step 2: Differential balance equation: \[ \frac{dQ}{dt} = \text{Rate In} - \text{Rate Out} = r_{\text{in}} c_{\text{in}} - r_{\text{out}} \frac{Q(t)}{V(t)} = 4(0.5) - 2 \frac{Q}{100 + 2t}. \] In standard linear form: \[ \frac{dQ}{dt} + \frac{1}{50 + t}Q = 2, \qquad Q(0) = 0. \]

Step 3: Integrating factor: \[ \mu(t) = \exp\left(\int \frac{1}{50 + t}\,dt\right) = 50 + t. \]

Step 4: Integrate and solve: \[ \frac{d}{dt}\big[(50 + t)Q\big] = 2(50 + t) \implies (50 + t)Q = (50 + t)^2 + C. \] Applying \( Q(0) = 0 \): \( 50(0) = 50^2 + C \implies C = -2500 \). Thus: \[ Q(t) = 50 + t - \frac{2500}{50 + t}. \]
body.ar:
A tank initially contains \( V_0 = 100 \text{ L} \) of fresh water. Brine with salt concentration \( c_{\text{in}} = 0.5 \text{ kg/L} \) flows in at \( r_{\text{in}} = 4 \text{ L/min} \). Well-mixed الحل is pumped out at \( r_{\text{out}} = 2 \text{ L/min} \). حدّد total salt mass \( Q(t) \) in the tank as a الدالة of time.

Step 1: Dynamic الحجم: Because \( r_{\text{in}} \neq r_{\text{out}} \), الحجم changes with time: \[ V(t) = V_0 + (r_{\text{in}} - r_{\text{out}})t = 100 + 2t. \]

Step 2: Differential balance المعادلة: \[ \frac{dQ}{dt} = \text{Rate In} - \text{Rate Out} = r_{\text{in}} c_{\text{in}} - r_{\text{out}} \frac{Q(t)}{V(t)} = 4(0.5) - 2 \frac{Q}{100 + 2t}. \] In standard linear form: \[ \frac{dQ}{dt} + \frac{1}{50 + t}Q = 2, \qquad Q(0) = 0. \]

Step 3: Integrating factor: \[ \mu(t) = \exp\left(\int \frac{1}{50 + t}\,dt\right) = 50 + t. \]

Step 4: Integrate and solve: \[ \frac{d}{dt}\big[(50 + t)Q\big] = 2(50 + t) \implies (50 + t)Q = (50 + t)^2 + C. \] Applying \( Q(0) = 0 \): \( 50(0) = 50^2 + C \implies C = -2500 \). وعليه: \[ Q(t) = 50 + t - \frac{2500}{50 + t}. \]

note.en: For constant coefficients \(P(x) = k\) and \(Q(x) = b\) with \(k > 0\), the integrating factor is \(e^{kx}\) and the exact solution is \(y(x) = b / k + (y0 - b/k)\)e^(-\(kx\)). The term \((y0 - b/k)\)e^(-\(kx\)) is the transient — it decays exponentially to 0 as \(x\) grows — leaving only the steady state \(y_{\text{inf}} = b / k\) (dashed amber line). Drag \(k\) to change the decay rate (a larger \(k\) pulls the curve toward the steady state faster; a smaller \(k\) lets the transient linger); drag \(b\) to shift the steady-state level; drag \(y_{0}\) to move the starting point above or below it.

label.en: ▲ Level 3 University Rigor — Theorem 2.2: Bernoulli Equations & Riccati Nonlinear Reduction
label.ar: ▲ Level 3 University Rigor — مبرهنة 2.2: Bernoulli المعادلات & Riccati Nonlinear Reduction

body.en:
1. Bernoulli Equations: An ODE of the form \[ \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)\,y = Q(x)\,y^n, \qquad n \in \mathbb{R}, \quad n \neq 0, 1 \] is nonlinear. Dividing by \( y^n \) yields \( y^{-n}y' + P(x)y^{1-n} = Q(x) \). Introducing the change of variable \[ v(x) = [y(x)]^{1-n} \implies \frac{dv}{dx} = (1 - n)y^{-n}\frac{dy}{dx} \] transforms the nonlinear ODE into an exact first-order linear ODE for \( v(x) \): \[ \frac{dv}{dx} + (1 - n)P(x)\,v = (1 - n)Q(x). \]

2. Riccati Equations: A quadratic first-order ODE of the form \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = q_0(x) + q_1(x)y + q_2(x)y^2, \qquad q_2(x) \neq 0 \] cannot generally be solved by quadratures. However:

  • If one particular solution \( y_1(x) \) is known, the substitution \( y(x) = y_1(x) + \frac{1}{v(x)} \) reduces the Riccati equation to a first-order linear ODE for \( v(x) \): \[ v' + \big(q_1(x) + 2q_2(x)y_1(x)\big)v = -q_2(x). \]
  • Alternatively, the substitution \( y(x) = -\frac{u'(x)}{q_2(x)u(x)} \) transforms the Riccati equation into a second-order linear homogeneous ODE: \[ u'' - \left(q_1(x) + \frac{q_2'(x)}{q_2(x)}\right)u' + q_0(x)q_2(x)u = 0. \]
body.ar:
1. Bernoulli المعادلات: An ODE of the form \[ \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)\,y = Q(x)\,y^n, \qquad n \in \mathbb{R}, \quad n \neq 0, 1 \] is nonlinear. Dividing by \( y^n \) yields \( y^{-n}y' + P(x)y^{1-n} = Q(x) \). Introducing the change of المتغير \[ v(x) = [y(x)]^{1-n} \implies \frac{dv}{dx} = (1 - n)y^{-n}\frac{dy}{dx} \] transforms the nonlinear ODE into an exact first-order linear ODE for \( v(x) \): \[ \frac{dv}{dx} + (1 - n)P(x)\,v = (1 - n)Q(x). \]

2. Riccati المعادلات: A quadratic first-order ODE of the form \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = q_0(x) + q_1(x)y + q_2(x)y^2, \qquad q_2(x) \neq 0 \] cannot generally be solved by quadratures. However:

  • If one particular الحل \( y_1(x) \) is known, the substitution \( y(x) = y_1(x) + \frac{1}{v(x)} \) reduces the Riccati المعادلة to a first-order linear ODE for \( v(x) \): \[ v' + \big(q_1(x) + 2q_2(x)y_1(x)\big)v = -q_2(x). \]
  • Alternatively, the substitution \( y(x) = -\frac{u'(x)}{q_2(x)u(x)} \) transforms the Riccati المعادلة into a second-order linear homogeneous ODE: \[ u'' - \left(q_1(x) + \frac{q_2'(x)}{q_2(x)}\right)u' + q_0(x)q_2(x)u = 0. \]

label.en: ⚠️ Common Traps & University Pitfalls — Standard Form & Integrating Factors
label.ar: ⚠️ أخطاء شائعة ومصائد جامعية — Standard Form & Integrating Factors

body.en:
Failure to normalize first: Never read \( P(x) \) directly from \( a(x)y' + b(x)y = c(x) \)! You must divide by \( a(x) \) first. If \( x y' + 2y = 4 \), \( P(x) = 2/x \), NOT \( 2 \). Using \( \mu = e^{2x} \) instead of \( x^2 \) is a catastrophic error.

Minus sign omissions: For \( y' - 3y = e^x \), \( P(x) = -3 \) and \( \mu(x) = e^{-3x} \). Dropping the negative sign results in \( \mu(x) = e^{3x} \), causing product-rule collapse to fail.

Exponent laws: \( \exp(3\ln x) = \exp(\ln x^3) = x^3 \). It is NOT \( 3x \) or \( 3\ln x \). Furthermore, remember to distribute the \( 1/\mu(x) \) across the constant \( C \): \( y = \frac{\int \mu Q\,dx}{\mu} + \frac{C}{\mu} \), never \( + C \) placed outside the fraction.
body.ar:

Minus sign omissions: For \( y' - 3y = e^x \), \( P(x) = -3 \) and \( \mu(x) = e^{-3x} \). Dropping the negative sign results in \( \mu(x) = e^{3x} \), causing product-rule collapse to fail.

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Linear First-Order Equations, Integrating Factors & Nonlinear Reductions (Hard Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(D\) — Linear First-Order المعادلات, Integrating Factors & Nonlinear Reductions (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): The Laplace transform of \( R(m) = 48e^{20m} \) is \( S(s) = \dfrac{48}{s - 20} \) for \( s > 20 \). Determine the evaluated transform \( S(21) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Substituting \( s = 21 \) gives \( \frac{48}{21 - 20} = 48 \).

question.en: Solve the initial value problem \( (x^2 + 1)\frac{dy}{dx} + 4x y = x \) with \( y(0) = 1 \).
question.ar: حل the initial value problem \( (x^2 + 1)\frac{dy}{dx} + 4x y = x \) with \( y(0) = 1 \).

solution.en:
Step 1: Normalize: \[ \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{4x}{x^2 + 1}y = \frac{x}{x^2 + 1}. \]

Step 2: Integrating factor: \[ \int P(x)\,dx = \int \frac{4x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx = 2\ln(x^2 + 1) = \ln\big((x^2 + 1)^2\big) \implies \mu(x) = (x^2 + 1)^2. \]

Step 3: Multiply and integrate: \[ \frac{d}{dx}\Big[(x^2 + 1)^2 y\Big] = (x^2 + 1)^2 \cdot \frac{x}{x^2 + 1} = x(x^2 + 1) = x^3 + x. \] Integrating: \[ (x^2 + 1)^2 y = \frac{x^4}{4} + \frac{x^2}{2} + C. \]

Step 4: Initial condition \( y(0) = 1 \): \[ (0 + 1)^2 (1) = 0 + 0 + C \implies C = 1. \]

Step 5: Particular solution: \[ y(x) = \frac{x^4/4 + x^2/2 + 1}{(x^2 + 1)^2} = \frac{x^4 + 2x^2 + 4}{4(x^2 + 1)^2} = \frac{(x^2 + 1)^2 + 3}{4(x^2 + 1)^2} = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{3}{4(x^2 + 1)^2}. \]
solution.ar:

question.en: Solve the nonlinear Bernoulli differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{1}{x}y = x y^2 \) for \( x > 0 \) with \( y(1) = -1 \).
question.ar: حل the nonlinear Bernoulli dإذا كانferential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{1}{x}y = x y^2 \) for \( x > 0 \) with \( y(1) = -1 \).

solution.en:
Step 1: Identify Bernoulli parameters: \( n = 2 \). Divide by \( y^2 \): \[ y^{-2}y' + \frac{1}{x}y^{-1} = x. \]

Step 2: Substitute \( v = y^{1-2} = y^{-1} \): \( v' = -y^{-2}y' \implies y^{-2}y' = -v' \). Substituting yields: \[ -v' + \frac{1}{x}v = x \implies v' - \frac{1}{x}v = -x. \]

Step 3: Integrating factor for linear equation in \( v \): \[ \mu(x) = \exp\left(\int -\frac{1}{x}\,dx\right) = e^{-\ln x} = \frac{1}{x}. \] Multiply through: \[ \frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{v}{x}\right] = \frac{1}{x}(-x) = -1 \implies \frac{v}{x} = -x + C \implies v(x) = C x - x^2. \]

Step 4: Revert to \( y \): \( y(x) = \frac{1}{v(x)} = \frac{1}{Cx - x^2} \).
Apply \( y(1) = -1 \): \( -1 = \frac{1}{C(1) - 1^2} = \frac{1}{C - 1} \implies C - 1 = -1 \implies C = 0 \).
Therefore: \[ y(x) = -\frac{1}{x^2}. \]
solution.ar:
Step 1: Identإذا كانy Bernoulli parameters: \( n = 2 \). Divide by \( y^2 \): \[ y^{-2}y' + \frac{1}{x}y^{-1} = x. \]

Step 3: Integrating حلّل for linear equation in \( v \): \[ \mu(x) = \exp\left(\int -\frac{1}{x}\,dx\right) = e^{-\ln x} = \frac{1}{x}. \] Multiply through: \[ \frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{v}{x}\right] = \frac{1}{x}(-x) = -1 \implies \frac{v}{x} = -x + C \implies v(x) = C x - x^2. \]

Step 4: Revert to \( y \): \( y(x) = \frac{1}{v(x)} = \frac{1}{Cx - x^2} \).
Apply \( y(1) = -1 \): \( -1 = \frac{1}{C(1) - 1^2} = \frac{1}{C - 1} \implies C - 1 = -1 \implies C = 0 \).
Therefore: \[ y(x) = -\frac{1}{x^2}. \]

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] Consider the linear first-order differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} + 2y = 6 \). If the initial condition is \( y(0) = 1 \), find the value of \( y(1) \).
question.ar: [Practice 3 · Easy] Consider the linear first-order dإذا كانferential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} + 2y = 6 \). إذا كان the initial condition is \( y(0) = 1 \), أوجد قيمة \( y(1) \).

hints.en: The given differential equation is a linear first-order ODE of the form \( \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x) \), where \( P(x) = 2 \) and \( Q(x) = 6 \). The integrating factor \( \mu(x) \) is given by \( \mu(x) = e^{\int P(x) dx} \).
hints.ar: The given dإذا كانferential equation is a linear first-order ODE of the form \( \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x) \), حيث \( P(x) = 2 \) and \( Q(x) = 6 \). The integrating حلّل \( \mu(x) \) is given by \( \mu(x) = e^{\int P(x) dx} \).

hints.en: Calculating the integrating factor: \( \mu(x) = e^{\int 2 dx} = e^{2x} \). Multiplying the differential equation by the integrating factor: \( e^{2x}\frac{dy}{dx} + 2e^{2x}y = 6e^{2x} \).
hints.ar: Calculating the integrating حلّل: \( \mu(x) = e^{\int 2 dx} = e^{2x} \). Multiplying the dإذا كانferential equation بتطبيق integrating حلّل: \( e^{2x}\frac{dy}{dx} + 2e^{2x}y = 6e^{2x} \).

solution.en:
The given differential equation is a linear first-order ODE of the form \( \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x) \), where \( P(x) = 2 \) and \( Q(x) = 6 \). The integrating factor \( \mu(x) \) is given by \( \mu(x) = e^{\int P(x) dx} \). 

Calculating the integrating factor: \( \mu(x) = e^{\int 2 dx} = e^{2x} \).

Multiplying the differential equation by the integrating factor: \( e^{2x}\frac{dy}{dx} + 2e^{2x}y = 6e^{2x} \).
The left side is the derivative of the product \( y\mu(x) \): \( \frac{d}{dx}(ye^{2x}) = 6e^{2x} \).

Integrating both sides with respect to \( x \): \( ye^{2x} = \int 6e^{2x} dx \).
\( ye^{2x} = 6 \cdot \frac{1}{2}e^{2x} + C \).
\( ye^{2x} = 3e^{2x} + C \).

Solving for \( y \): \( y = 3 + Ce^{-2x} \).

Using the initial condition \( y(0) = 1 \) to find \( C \): \( 1 = 3 + Ce^{-2(0)} \).
\( 1 = 3 + C \).
\( C = 1 - 3 = -2 \).

So, the particular solution is \( y(x) = 3 - 2e^{-2x} \).

Now, we need to find \( y(1) \): \( y(1) = 3 - 2e^{-2(1)} = 3 - 2e^{-2} \).

This matches choice C.
solution.ar:
The given dإذا كانferential equation is a linear first-order ODE of the form \( \frac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x) \), حيث \( P(x) = 2 \) and \( Q(x) = 6 \). The integrating حلّل \( \mu(x) \) is given by \( \mu(x) = e^{\int P(x) dx} \). 

Calculating the integrating حلّل: \( \mu(x) = e^{\int 2 dx} = e^{2x} \).

Multiplying the dإذا كانferential equation بتطبيق integrating حلّل: \( e^{2x}\frac{dy}{dx} + 2e^{2x}y = 6e^{2x} \).
The left side is the derivative of the product \( y\mu(x) \): \( \frac{d}{dx}(ye^{2x}) = 6e^{2x} \).

Integrating both sides بالنسبة إلى \( x \): \( ye^{2x} = \int 6e^{2x} dx \).
\( ye^{2x} = 6 \cdot \frac{1}{2}e^{2x} + C \).
\( ye^{2x} = 3e^{2x} + C \).

Solving for \( y \): \( y = 3 + Ce^{-2x} \).

باستخدام initial condition \( y(0) = 1 \) to أوجد \( C \): \( 1 = 3 + Ce^{-2(0)} \).
\( 1 = 3 + C \).
\( C = 1 - 3 = -2 \).

So, the particular solution is \( y(x) = 3 - 2e^{-2x} \).

Now, we need to أوجد \( y(1) \): \( y(1) = 3 - 2e^{-2(1)} = 3 - 2e^{-2} \).

This matches choice C.

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law
label.ar: ● الأطلس الشامل للدوال الأم التسع وقانون التحويلات الهندسية العام

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
body.ar:
تُبنى النماذج الجبرية والمتسامية الأساسية من خلال تطبيق التحويل القياسي \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\) على إحدى الدوال الأم التسع، حيث يتحكم \(|a|\) في التمدد الرأسي (مع انعكاس حول محور السينات إذا كان \(a < 0\))، ويمثل \(h\) الإزاحة الأفقية، و\(k\) الإزاحة الرأسية:

عائلة الدالةالصورة المحوّلة \(g(x)\)المجالالمدى (\(a > 0\))السمة الهندسية المميزة
الثابتة\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)مستقيم أفقي ميله \(0\)
الخطية\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)ميل ثابت \(m = a\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, k)\)
التربيعية\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)قطع مكافئ رأسه \((h, k)\) ومحوره \(x = h\)
التكعيبية\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)نقطة انعطاف مركزية \((h, k)\)
القيمة المطلقة\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)رأس زاوي على شكل V عند \((h, k)\) بميلين \(\pm a\)
الجذرية\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)نقطة بداية \((h, k)\) ومجال مقيّد \(x \ge h\)
النسبية (المقلوب)\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) وتقارب أفقي \(y = k\)
